name: Othni
overview: Othni was a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as the son of Shemaiah. His mention in Scripture is concise, with no additional notes or details beyond his lineage. As a Levite, Othni belonged to the priestly tribe set apart for service to God.
namesAndTitles: The name Othni appears as a proper name in Scripture without any provided meaning or divine naming indication. There is only one recorded instance of this name, found in 1 Chronicles 26:7.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Othni was the son of Shemaiah. No other family relationships are documented for him beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Othni's significance lies primarily in his genealogical connection within the Levitical lineage. Being a son of Shemaiah situates him within the tribe responsible for the temple service and religious duties in Israel. Although little else is recorded about him, his mention preserves the continuity of the Levitical family lines important for understanding priestly roles and heritage.
